taskDescription: A child with acute diarrhoea is given oral rehydration solution. To understand why it works, arrange these membrane transport mechanisms from the one requiring NO energy to the one requiring the MOST energy and machinery.
paragraphs: Simple diffusion: small non-polar molecules such as O₂ and CO₂ dissolve through the lipid bilayer down their concentration gradient without any protein.
Facilitated diffusion via channels: ions move through gated protein pores such as aquaporins down their electrochemical gradient, with no energy spent.
Facilitated diffusion via carriers: a substrate binds a carrier protein such as GLUT4 that changes shape; movement is still downhill, saturable and specific, but requires no ATP.
Primary active transport: the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase uses one ATP to pump 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in, moving ions against their concentration gradient.
Secondary active transport: SGLT1 carries glucose uphill into the intestinal cell by coupling it to sodium moving downhill on the gradient the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase maintains.
Vesicular transport: endocytosis and exocytosis move large particles or bulk fluid in membrane-bound vesicles, requiring ATP, cytoskeletal machinery and membrane fusion.

overallFeedback.feedback: Transport mechanisms form a hierarchy of energy cost: passive processes (simple and facilitated diffusion) use no ATP; primary active transport spends ATP directly; secondary active transport (e.g. SGLT1 in ORS) spends it indirectly via the sodium gradient; and vesicular transport needs ATP plus cytoskeletal and membrane-fusion machinery.
